function.mechanism: Provides intense sweetness at low use levels and is used as a general-purpose sweetener/flavor enhancer in formulated foods.

adi.basis: EFSA FAF Panel 2025 re-evaluation; ADI of 15 mg/kg bw/day replaced the SCF 2000 ADI of 9 mg/kg bw/day.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA reported highest EU exposure estimates generally below ADI across population groups (no safety concern) and recommended tighter impurity specifications.

fda.notes: Regulated as an approved food additive (not GRAS listing in Part 184 search); allowed as a general-purpose sweetener and flavor enhancer except in meat and poultry under cGMP, with identity/specification conditions including >=99% purity.

adi.basis: JECFA database entry shows ADI range 0-15 mg/kg bw (Meeting 46; TRS 806).

concerns.summary: A 2024 study reported higher central precocious puberty risk with higher acesulfame potassium intake in girls, supported by experimental neuroendocrine findings; causality remains uncertain due observational design limits.
A 2022 study reported associations with preterm-risk/uterine contractility and supporting experimental signaling data, primarily under high-dose and mixed-method settings.
A 2026 mechanistic study found synergistic nephrotoxicity signals for benzoic-acid and acesulfame-K co-exposure in vitro (CTNNB1/STAT3 axis).
Recent reviews describe preclinical microbiome and metabolic pathway perturbation signals, often at supraphysiologic or context-specific exposure levels.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2025 set ADI at 15 mg/kg bw/day and reported highest exposure estimates generally below ADI with no population-level safety concern in its assessment.
Recent reviews of nonsugar sweeteners reported no consistent human-relevant carcinogenic signal for acesulfame potassium.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2025 reported highest EU exposure estimates for E950 were generally below the ADI in all population groups.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evidence remains dominant: EFSA, FDA (CFR), and JECFA maintain approval with defined ADI/GMP constraints, and EFSA's 2025 exposure assessment did not indicate ADI exceedance. Newer endocrine/reproductive and co-exposure mechanistic findings are important but not yet sufficient to shift risk to moderate/high under current regulatory interpretation.
key_factors: EFSA 2025 ADI is 15 mg/kg bw/day with highest modeled exposure generally below ADI.
US status is approved under 21 CFR 172.800 with use and specification conditions.
JECFA ADI remains 0-15 mg/kg bw in database entry.
No acesulfame entry identified in current IARC classification dataset.
Recent studies suggest potential endocrine/reproductive and mixture-toxicity concerns that warrant monitoring.
